claims.text: The starting powder blend is equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling induces high lattice strain in CoCrFeNiTi.
Approximately 6 hours of high-energy ball milling refines the CoCrFeNiTi grain size to below 100 nm.
Milling-induced lattice strain and grain refinement lower the energy barrier for a BCC-to-FCC solid-solution transition.
Valence electron concentration governs BCC/FCC phase stability in CoCrFeNiTi.
Atomic-radius mismatch governs BCC/FCC phase stability in CoCrFeNiTi.
The structural mediator after milling is a nanocrystalline BCC solid solution with high dislocation density and grain-boundary area.
The proposed SPS treatment is above 1000°C for 10 minutes under 50 MPa.
SPS under the proposed conditions produces more than 98% theoretical density.
The proposed SPS cycle suppresses excessive precipitation of HCP Ti-rich phases.
The high defect density and nanocrystalline structure of the milled state thermodynamically favor FCC formation at elevated temperature.
The rapid SPS cycle and stabilized nanocrystalline matrix kinetically retain Ti in solid solution.
The sintered alloy will have a dual-phase FCC/BCC microstructure.
The sintered alloy will have an average grain size below 500 nm.
The sintered alloy will exceed 600 HV at a 10 g Vickers load.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has hardness of approximately 200 HV.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has more than 5% porosity.
Cast CoCrFeNiTi has a coarse grain structure exceeding 10 μm.
SPS above 1100°C causes excessive grain growth beyond 1 μm and decomposition into brittle intermetallic phases.
Significant Vickers-hardness load dependence between 10 g and 50 g indicates precipitation hardening and would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis assigns the key transition to approximately 6 hours of milling, but elsewhere specifies an optimized duration and states that the exact duration may require adjustment, weakening the status of 6 hours as a defined intervention.
